summary: Willem Bollée was an Indologist who studied at Utrecht University (~1946–1956) and completed his Habilitation at the University of Hamburg (~1972–1975). He was an assistant professor at the University of Münster (1971–1978) and taught at Heidelberg University (~1970–1993).

Indologist Willem Caland earned his doctorate at Leiden University (1877), studying under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern and Carel Gabriel Cobet. He held posts at Utrecht University as lecturer (1903) and Chair of Sanskrit (1906–1929), and at Leiden University (1913–1914).

Willem van der Molen worked in linguistics, history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Leiden University (~1970–1983) and later held posts at Leiden University (~1979–2017) and the University of Indonesia.
William Blackstone studied at Charterhouse School (~1735–1738) and Pembroke College, Oxford (~1738–1745). He later held a post at the University of Oxford (~1753–1766).

William C. Chittick works in religious studies and philosophy. After studying at the University of Tehran (~1966–1974), he held positions at Sharif University of Technology (~1970–1978), University at Albany, SUNY (~1980–1983), and Stony Brook University (~1983).

Sinologist and historian William C. Kirby studied at Dartmouth College and Harvard University under Philip A. Kuhn. He held posts at Washington University in St. Louis (~1980–1992) and Harvard University (from 1992), with visiting professorships at Heidelberg and Berlin.

William Carey was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ram Ram Basu and Golok Nath Sharma. In 1801, he became Professor of Sanskrit at Fort William College, and he founded BMS World Mission, Serampore College, and several societies.

Linguist and Indologist William Dwight Whitney studied at Williams College, Yale, Berlin, and Tübingen under Salisbury, Weber, Roth, and Lepsius. He spent his career at Yale (1853, 1869–1894) and served in multiple roles for the American Oriental Society.

William Edelglass works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He has taught philosophy at Colby College (attested 2007) and held positions as a professor at Marlboro College (attested 2013) and visiting professor at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics.

Sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar William Edward Soothill studied at the University of London. He served as president of Shanxi University (1911) and was appointed Professor of Chinese at the University of Oxford in 1920.

William Erskine worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history and archaeology. He was educated at the Royal High School, Edinburgh, and studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1787–1792).
William Evans Hoyle was educated at Christ Church, University of Oxford, where he studied from around 1874 to 1877, and also studied at the University of Manchester.

William F. Powell is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He has held positions at the University of California, Santa Barbara (attested 1986, 2026), where he became Emeritus Professor of Religious Studies and Research Professor.
William Frederic Sinclair worked in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the Royal School Dungannon and Armagh, and entered the Indian Civil Service in 1866.

Sinologist William H. Nienhauser, Jr. studied at Indiana University under Irving Yucheng Lo and Friedrich Alexander Bischoff, and at Bonn. After visiting roles, he became a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (from 1983; Halls-Bascom Professor from 1995).

Indologist and Buddhist scholar William Henry Denham Rouse studied at Cheltenham College, Regent's Park College, and Cambridge. He held teaching posts at Bedford, Cheltenham, and Rugby, and served as headmaster of The Perse School (1902–1928).

William Herschel held posts with the Hanoverian Foot Guards (~1753–1758), County Durham Militia (1760–1761), Charles Avison (1761–1762), Leeds (1762–1766), Octagon Chapel, Bath (1767–1780), Bath Philharmonia (1780–1782), and Observatory House (1782–1822).

William Hodge Mill worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1809–1813), served as Principal of Bishop's College, Kolkata (~1820–1838), and held a post at the University of Cambridge (~1848–1853).
William Homan Thorpe studied at Jesus College, Cambridge (~1921–1925). He later held a post at the University of Cambridge from approximately 1932 to 1969.

William James worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Plymouth College and Harvard (including Harvard Medical School, 1864–1869). He held successive Harvard appointments in physiology and philosophy from 1872, becoming full professor in 1885.
